chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah who said:

The false testifiers are whipped with a penalty (hadd) that has no fixed time; that is up to the Imam, and they are paraded until they are recognized, so they do not repeat. I said to him, 'So if they repent and improve, will their testimony be accepted afterwards?' He said: 'When they repent, Allah turns to them with mercy, and their testimony is accepted afterwards.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment and legal status of false witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the judicial procedure for false witnesses (shuhud al-zur), prescribing a discretionary whipping (ta'zir) determined by the Imam, accompanied by public parading to ensure recognition and deterrence. It highlights the Shia legal principle that while the penalty is severe, sincere repentance (tawbah) restores the witness's credibility, reflecting the divine mercy that 'if they repent, Allah repents to them.'

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at who said,

‘The false testifiers would be whipped a Penalty (Hadd), there being no timing for it, that is up to the Imamasws, and they would be paraded with until they are recognised as such, so they would not repeat’. I said to himasws, ‘So if they repent and be correct, would their testimonies be accepted afterwards?’ Heasws said: ‘When they repent, Allahazwj would Turn to them (with Mercy), and their testimonies would be accepted afterwards’.
